name: Frontal bone
function: Forms the forehead, the roof of each orbit and the floor of the anterior cranial fossa; houses the frontal sinuses.

details.label: Articulates with
details.value: Parietals (coronal suture), sphenoid, ethmoid, nasal, maxilla, zygomatic, lacrimal

details.label: Key features
details.value: Supraorbital margin and foramen/notch, glabella, frontal eminences, orbital plates, frontal sinus

details.label: Foramina & contents
details.value: Supraorbital foramen – supraorbital nerve (V1) and vessels

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Orbicularis oculi (orbital part, nasal part of frontal bone), corrugator supercilii (superciliary arch), temporalis (temporal fossa); frontalis has no bony attachment, inserting into skin via the galea

pearl: Anterior cranial fossa fracture: CSF rhinorrhea, raccoon eyes and anosmia from olfactory fibers torn at the cribriform plate.

name: Parietal bone
function: Paired bones forming the roof and sides of the cranial vault; protect the cerebral hemispheres and anchor the temporalis.

details.label: Articulates with
details.value: Frontal (coronal), opposite parietal (sagittal), occipital (lambdoid), temporal (squamous), sphenoid

details.label: Key features
details.value: Parietal eminence, superior and inferior temporal lines, internal grooves for middle meningeal artery

details.label: Foramina & contents
details.value: Parietal foramen – emissary vein to the superior sagittal sinus

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Temporalis (inferior temporal line), temporal fascia (superior temporal line)

pearl: Emissary veins through the parietal foramen link scalp veins to the superior sagittal sinus, a route for scalp infection to cause intracranial sinus thrombosis.

name: Temporal bone
function: Forms the lateral skull base and side of the vault; houses the middle and inner ear and transmits CN VII, CN VIII and the internal carotid artery.

details.label: Parts
details.value: Squamous, tympanic, petrous (with mastoid), zygomatic process, styloid process

details.label: Articulates with
details.value: Parietal, occipital, sphenoid, zygomatic, mandible (TMJ)

details.label: Foramina & contents
details.value: Internal acoustic meatus (CN VII, VIII, labyrinthine a.), carotid canal (ICA), stylomastoid foramen (CN VII), jugular foramen (shared with occipital)

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Temporalis, masseter (zygomatic process), SCM, splenius and longissimus capitis, digastric (mastoid), styloid muscles

pearl: Temporal bone fracture: hemotympanum, Battle sign, CSF otorrhea, facial palsy and hearing loss; transverse fractures injure CN VII/VIII more often than longitudinal.

name: Occipital bone
function: Forms the posterior and inferior skull; encloses the foramen magnum and articulates with the atlas, carrying the head on the spine.

details.label: Articulates with
details.value: Parietals (lambdoid), temporals, sphenoid (spheno-occipital synchondrosis at the clivus), atlas (occipital condyles)

details.label: Key features
details.value: External occipital protuberance, nuchal lines, occipital condyles, clivus, internal grooves for transverse sinuses

details.label: Foramina & contents
details.value: Foramen magnum (medulla, vertebral arteries, CN XI spinal roots), hypoglossal canal (CN XII), condylar canal (emissary vein)

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Trapezius, SCM, splenius capitis, semispinalis capitis, suboccipital muscles, ligamentum nuchae

pearl: Occipital condyle fracture and atlanto-occipital dislocation follow high-energy trauma; dislocation is frequently fatal from brainstem injury.

name: Sphenoid bone
function: Butterfly-shaped keystone of the skull base joining all cranial fossae; holds the pituitary in the sella turcica and transmits CN II–VI.

details.label: Parts
details.value: Body (sphenoid sinus, sella turcica), lesser wings, greater wings, pterygoid processes

details.label: Articulates with
details.value: All other cranial bones plus zygomatic, palatine and vomer

details.label: Foramina & contents
details.value: Optic canal (CN II, ophthalmic a.), superior orbital fissure (III, IV, V1, VI, ophthalmic veins), rotundum (V2), ovale (V3), spinosum (middle meningeal a.)

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Temporalis, lateral and medial pterygoids, tensor veli palatini, superior constrictor (pterygoid hamulus/raphe)

pearl: Transsphenoidal pituitary surgery reaches the sella through the sphenoid sinus; the adjacent cavernous sinus puts the ICA and CN III–VI at risk.

name: Ethmoid bone
function: Fragile midline bone between the orbits forming the nasal roof, medial orbital wall and upper septum; its cribriform plate carries olfactory nerves.

details.label: Parts
details.value: Cribriform plate, crista galli, perpendicular plate, lamina papyracea, ethmoid air cells, superior and middle conchae

details.label: Articulates with
details.value: Frontal, sphenoid, nasal, maxilla, lacrimal, palatine, vomer, inferior nasal concha

details.label: Foramina & contents
details.value: Cribriform foramina – CN I filaments; anterior/posterior ethmoidal foramina – ethmoidal nerves (V1) and arteries

details.label: Key relation
details.value: Lamina papyracea is the paper-thin wall between ethmoid cells and the orbit

pearl: Ethmoid sinusitis spreads through the lamina papyracea to cause orbital cellulitis in children: proptosis, painful ophthalmoplegia, risk of cavernous sinus thrombosis.

name: Nasal bone
function: Paired small bones forming the bridge of the nose; support the upper nasal dorsum and meet the frontal bone at the nasion.

details.label: Articulates with
details.value: Frontal bone, opposite nasal bone, maxilla (frontal process), ethmoid (perpendicular plate)

details.label: Key features
details.value: Nasion at the frontonasal suture; groove for the external nasal nerve (V1)

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Upper lateral nasal cartilages below; procerus and nasalis overlie it

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Dorsal nasal (ophthalmic) and angular (facial) arteries

pearl: Most commonly fractured facial bone; always look for a septal hematoma, which must be drained to prevent cartilage necrosis and saddle-nose deformity.

name: Lacrimal bone
function: Smallest facial bone, in the anteromedial orbital wall; forms the lacrimal fossa for the lacrimal sac and the groove of the nasolacrimal duct.

details.label: Articulates with
details.value: Frontal, ethmoid, maxilla, inferior nasal concha

details.label: Key features
details.value: Lacrimal fossa (lacrimal sac), posterior lacrimal crest, nasolacrimal groove

details.label: Related drainage
details.value: Nasolacrimal duct empties into the inferior meatus beneath the inferior concha

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Lacrimal part of orbicularis oculi (posterior lacrimal crest), medial palpebral ligament nearby

pearl: Nasolacrimal duct obstruction causes epiphora and dacryocystitis (tender medial canthal swelling); treated with probing or dacryocystorhinostomy.

name: Zygomatic bone
function: Cheekbone forming the lateral orbital wall and part of the orbital floor and zygomatic arch; transmits masseter forces to the skull.

details.label: Articulates with
details.value: Frontal, sphenoid (greater wing), temporal (zygomatic process), maxilla

details.label: Key features
details.value: Frontal, temporal and maxillary processes; orbital surface; malar prominence

details.label: Foramina & contents
details.value: Zygomaticofacial and zygomaticotemporal foramina – cutaneous branches of V2

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Masseter, zygomaticus major and minor, temporal fascia

pearl: Zygomaticomaxillary complex (tripod) fracture: flattened cheek, trismus, infraorbital numbness and diplopia from orbital floor involvement.

name: Maxilla
function: Upper jaw forming the orbital floor, nasal floor and lateral wall, anterior hard palate and upper alveolar arch; contains the maxillary sinus.

details.label: Articulates with
details.value: Frontal, ethmoid, nasal, lacrimal, zygomatic, palatine, vomer, inferior concha, opposite maxilla

details.label: Key features
details.value: Frontal, zygomatic, palatine and alveolar processes; maxillary sinus (largest paranasal sinus) draining to the middle meatus

details.label: Foramina & contents
details.value: Infraorbital foramen – infraorbital nerve (V2) and vessels; incisive canal – nasopalatine nerve and sphenopalatine artery branches

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Buccinator, levator anguli oris, levator labii superioris, nasalis, orbicularis oris

pearl: Le Fort fractures all pass through the pterygoid plates: I floating palate, II pyramidal through the nasal bridge, III craniofacial dysjunction with CSF leak.

name: Palatine bone
function: L-shaped bone forming the posterior hard palate, part of the lateral nasal wall and orbital floor; its perpendicular plate forms the medial wall of the pterygopalatine fossa.

details.label: Articulates with
details.value: Maxilla, sphenoid, ethmoid, vomer, inferior nasal concha, opposite palatine

details.label: Key features
details.value: Horizontal plate (posterior quarter of hard palate; maxillary palatine processes form the anterior three-quarters), perpendicular plate, orbital and sphenoidal processes, pyramidal process

details.label: Foramina & contents
details.value: Greater palatine foramen – greater palatine nerve and artery; lesser palatine foramina – lesser palatine nerves and vessels; sphenopalatine foramen (notch closed by sphenoid body) – sphenopalatine artery and nasopalatine nerve

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Palatine aponeurosis (tensor/levator veli palatini), musculus uvulae (posterior nasal spine), medial pterygoid (pyramidal process)

pearl: The sphenopalatine foramen transmits the sphenopalatine artery, the source of posterior epistaxis that fails anterior packing and may need embolization or ligation.

name: Inferior nasal concha
function: Separate curved bone projecting into the nasal cavity as the largest turbinate; warms and humidifies air and roofs the inferior meatus.

details.label: Articulates with
details.value: Maxilla, palatine, lacrimal, ethmoid

details.label: Key features
details.value: Covered by thick erectile mucosa with venous sinusoids; inferior meatus beneath receives the nasolacrimal duct

details.label: Related
details.value: Superior and middle conchae are parts of the ethmoid, not separate bones

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Nasal mucoperiosteum only

pearl: Inferior turbinate hypertrophy (allergic or vasomotor rhinitis) causes nasal obstruction; the nasolacrimal duct opens beneath it, so tears drain into the nose.

name: Vomer
function: Thin midline plate forming the posteroinferior nasal septum; separates the two choanae.

details.label: Articulates with
details.value: Sphenoid (rostrum), ethmoid (perpendicular plate), maxillae and palatines (nasal crest), septal cartilage

details.label: Key features
details.value: Alae clasp the sphenoid rostrum; groove for the nasopalatine nerve and sphenopalatine vessels

details.label: Septum components
details.value: Septal cartilage (anterior), perpendicular plate of ethmoid (superior), vomer (posteroinferior)

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Septal cartilage anteriorly, nasal mucosa

pearl: Deviated septum involving the vomer causes unilateral obstruction; septoplasty must preserve a dorsal and caudal cartilage strut to avoid saddle-nose collapse.

name: Mandible
function: Lower jaw, the only mobile skull bone; bears the lower teeth and articulates with the temporal bone at the TMJ for mastication and speech.

details.label: Articulates with
details.value: Temporal bone at the temporomandibular joints (bilateral)

details.label: Key features
details.value: Body, ramus, angle, condylar and coronoid processes, alveolar process, mental protuberance, mylohyoid line, lingula

details.label: Foramina & contents
details.value: Mandibular foramen – inferior alveolar nerve, artery, vein; mental foramen – mental nerve and vessels

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Masseter, temporalis, medial and lateral pterygoids, mylohyoid, geniohyoid, genioglossus, digastric, buccinator, platysma

pearl: The mandible is a ring, so fractures are usually double (angle plus contralateral parasymphysis). Check for inferior alveolar/mental nerve numbness and malocclusion.

name: Temporomandibular joint (TMJ)
function: Synovial hinge-and-glide joint between the mandibular condyle and temporal articular fossa; a fibrocartilage disc splits it into rotation (lower) and translation (upper) compartments.

details.label: Articulates with
details.value: Mandibular condyle with the mandibular (glenoid) fossa and articular eminence of the temporal bone

details.label: Key features
details.value: Fibrocartilage articular disc; lateral (temporomandibular), sphenomandibular and stylomandibular ligaments

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Auriculotemporal and masseteric nerves (V3)

details.label: Movements
details.value: Depression (lateral pterygoid, digastric, gravity), elevation (masseter, temporalis, medial pterygoid), protrusion, retrusion, lateral excursion

pearl: Anterior dislocation: wide yawning lets the condyle slip over the articular eminence; jaw locks open. Reduce with gloved thumbs pressing down then back on the molars.

name: Condylar process
function: Posterosuperior projection of the ramus whose head articulates in the TMJ; its neck receives the lateral pterygoid and is the weakest point of the ramus.

details.label: Location
details.value: Posterior border of the ramus; with the mouth closed the head sits in the mandibular fossa, posterior to the articular tubercle, and glides forward onto the tubercle on opening

details.label: Key features
details.value: Head (condyle), neck, pterygoid fovea; separated from coronoid by the mandibular notch

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Lateral pterygoid (pterygoid fovea and articular disc), TMJ capsule

details.label: Relations
details.value: Auriculotemporal nerve, superficial temporal and maxillary arteries, parotid gland, external acoustic meatus behind

pearl: Condylar neck fracture from a blow to the chin: ramus shortens, giving ipsilateral premature molar contact with a CONTRALATERAL open bite; chin deviates toward the fractured side on opening. Often managed closed.

name: Coronoid process
function: Anterior triangular projection of the ramus that receives the temporalis tendon; lies deep to the zygomatic arch.

details.label: Location
details.value: Anterosuperior ramus, separated from the condyle by the mandibular (sigmoid) notch

details.label: Key features
details.value: Thin flattened process; masseteric nerve and vessels cross the notch behind it

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Temporalis tendon (medial and lateral surfaces)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Zygomatic arch and masseter laterally, buccal nerve medially

pearl: A depressed zygomatic arch fracture impinges on the coronoid process causing trismus; the Gillies approach elevates the arch deep to the temporal fascia.

name: Ramus of mandible
function: Vertical plate between the angle and the condyle; site of the mandibular foramen and of masseter and medial pterygoid insertion (pterygomasseteric sling).

details.label: Location
details.value: Posterior mandible from the angle up to the condylar and coronoid processes

details.label: Key features
details.value: Mandibular foramen guarded by the lingula on the medial surface, mylohyoid groove, masseteric tuberosity

details.label: Foramina & contents
details.value: Mandibular foramen – inferior alveolar nerve, artery and vein entering the mandibular canal

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Masseter (lateral), medial pterygoid (medial), sphenomandibular ligament (lingula), parotid gland overlies it

pearl: Inferior alveolar nerve block: needle contacts the medial ramus at the mandibular foramen; aspirate to avoid intravascular injection; lingual nerve lies just anterior.

name: Angle of mandible
function: Posteroinferior corner (gonion) where body meets ramus; gripped by the pterygomasseteric sling and crossed anteriorly by the facial vessels.

details.label: Location
details.value: Junction of body and ramus; angle ~120° in adults, more obtuse in infants and the edentulous

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Masseter (lateral), medial pterygoid (medial), stylomandibular ligament, platysma

details.label: Relations
details.value: Facial artery and vein cross the inferior border just anterior to it at the anterior edge of masseter; marginal mandibular branch of CN VII runs along the border; parotid tail behind

details.label: Key features
details.value: Everted in males, inverted in females

pearl: With the condyle, one of the two commonest mandibular fracture sites (weakened by an impacted third molar). Incisions near the inferior border risk the marginal mandibular branch of CN VII (drooping lip).

name: Body of mandible
function: Horizontal horseshoe portion carrying the lower teeth; its inner surface anchors the floor-of-mouth muscles and its outer surface the lip depressors.

details.label: Location
details.value: From the symphysis menti to the angle on each side

details.label: Key features
details.value: Mental protuberance, oblique line, mylohyoid line, digastric fossa, genial tubercles, sublingual and submandibular fossae

details.label: Foramina & contents
details.value: Mental foramen – mental nerve and vessels (below the second premolar)

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Mylohyoid, geniohyoid, genioglossus, anterior digastric, buccinator, depressor anguli oris, depressor labii inferioris, mentalis, platysma

pearl: Ludwig angina: infected 2nd/3rd molar roots lie below the mylohyoid line, so pus spreads to the submandibular space with woody floor-of-mouth swelling and airway risk.

name: Alveolar process of mandible
function: Tooth-bearing ridge on the upper border of the mandibular body holding the lower dentition in sockets; resorbs after tooth loss.

details.label: Location
details.value: Superior border of the mandibular body from the incisors to the third molar

details.label: Key features
details.value: Sockets (alveoli) for 16 lower teeth, interalveolar septa, periodontal ligament, buccal and lingual cortical plates

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Inferior alveolar nerve (V3); lingual gingiva by lingual nerve; buccal gingiva by buccal and mental nerves

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Buccinator along the molar region externally; gingiva

pearl: Edentulous resorption brings the mental foramen to the crest, causing denture pain; dry socket (alveolar osteitis) follows clot loss 3–5 days after extraction.

name: Hyoid bone
function: U-shaped bone suspended in the anterior neck at C3 by muscles and ligaments; anchors the tongue, floor of mouth and larynx and has no bony articulation.

details.label: Location
details.value: Anterior neck at C3, in the angle between the mandible and thyroid cartilage

details.label: Key features
details.value: Body, greater horns, lesser horns; stylohyoid ligament to the styloid process

details.label: Attachments (suprahyoid)
details.value: Mylohyoid, geniohyoid, hyoglossus, digastric (via sling), stylohyoid, middle constrictor

details.label: Attachments (infrahyoid)
details.value: Sternohyoid, omohyoid, thyrohyoid, thyrohyoid membrane

pearl: Hyoid fracture is rare and strongly suggests manual strangulation. Thyroglossal duct cysts pass through or behind the hyoid and rise with tongue protrusion.

name: Thyroid cartilage
function: Largest laryngeal cartilage; two laminae fused at the laryngeal prominence shield the vocal cords, which attach to its inner surface.

details.label: Location
details.value: C4–C5, between the hyoid above and cricoid below

details.label: Key features
details.value: Laryngeal prominence (Adam's apple), thyroid notch, superior and inferior horns, oblique line

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Thyrohyoid membrane, cricothyroid, thyrohyoid, sternothyroid, inferior constrictor, vocal ligaments, thyroepiglottic ligament

details.label: Type
details.value: Hyaline cartilage, ossifies with age

pearl: Cricothyroidotomy: from the laryngeal prominence, slide a finger down the midline to the soft dip between thyroid cartilage and cricoid arch (cricothyroid membrane). Carotid bifurcation is at its upper border.

name: Cricoid cartilage
function: Only complete cartilage ring of the airway (signet-ring shape) at C6; supports the arytenoids and is the narrowest point of the pediatric airway.

details.label: Location
details.value: C6, between the thyroid cartilage and first tracheal ring

details.label: Key features
details.value: Narrow anterior arch, broad posterior lamina; facets for the arytenoids and inferior thyroid horns

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Cricothyroid, posterior and lateral cricoarytenoids, cricothyroid membrane, cricotracheal ligament, inferior constrictor

details.label: C6 relations
details.value: Pharynx becomes esophagus, larynx becomes trachea, carotid tubercle, vertebral artery enters transverse foramen

pearl: Cricoid pressure (Sellick) compresses the esophagus during rapid sequence intubation. Croup and post-intubation subglottic stenosis narrow the airway at this level.

name: Epiglottis
function: Leaf-shaped elastic cartilage behind the tongue base that folds over the laryngeal inlet during swallowing, diverting food into the piriform recesses.

details.label: Location
details.value: Posterior to the hyoid and tongue root; stalk (petiole) attaches inside the thyroid cartilage

details.label: Key features
details.value: Elastic cartilage (never ossifies); valleculae in front; aryepiglottic folds at its sides

details.label: Innervation of mucosa
details.value: Internal laryngeal nerve (CN X); lingual surface partly CN IX

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Thyroepiglottic and hyoepiglottic ligaments, median glossoepiglottic fold, aryepiglottic muscles

pearl: Acute epiglottitis (H. influenzae b, streptococci): drooling, tripod posture, muffled voice, thumbprint sign on lateral neck film; secure the airway before examining.

name: Arytenoid cartilages
function: Paired pyramidal cartilages on the cricoid lamina whose rotation and gliding abduct, adduct and tension the vocal cords.

details.label: Location
details.value: Posterior larynx, atop the cricoid lamina

details.label: Key features
details.value: Vocal process (vocal ligament), muscular process (cricoarytenoid muscles), apex (corniculate cartilage)

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Posterior cricoarytenoid (sole abductor), lateral cricoarytenoid, transverse and oblique arytenoids, thyroarytenoid, vocalis

details.label: Innervation of muscles
details.value: Recurrent laryngeal nerve (CN X); cricothyroid alone by external laryngeal nerve

pearl: Arytenoid dislocation after intubation mimics recurrent laryngeal palsy (hoarseness, immobile cord); laryngeal EMG distinguishes it and closed reduction fixes it.

name: Tracheal rings
function: 16–20 C-shaped hyaline cartilage rings keep the trachea patent; the open posterior gap is closed by the trachealis muscle against the esophagus.

details.label: Location
details.value: From C6 (below the cricoid) to the carina at T4–T5

details.label: Key features
details.value: Incomplete posteriorly; first ring is broadest; joined by annular ligaments

details.label: Relations in neck
details.value: Thyroid isthmus over rings 2–4, inferior thyroid veins, brachiocephalic trunk at the thoracic inlet, recurrent laryngeal nerves in the tracheoesophageal grooves

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Trachealis, esophagus posteriorly, pretracheal fascia

pearl: Tracheostomy is placed through rings 2–4 below the thyroid isthmus; cricothyroidotomy is faster in emergencies. Tracheomalacia follows prolonged intubation or goiter.

name: Atlas (C1)
function: Ring-shaped C1 with no body or spinous process; its lateral masses carry the skull and permit nodding at the atlanto-occipital joints.

details.label: Articulates with
details.value: Occipital condyles above; axis (lateral facets and dens) below

details.label: Key features
details.value: Anterior and posterior arches, lateral masses, long transverse processes, transverse foramina, groove for the vertebral artery on the posterior arch

details.label: Ligaments
details.value: Transverse ligament of the atlas holds the dens against the anterior arch

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Rectus capitis anterior and lateralis, obliquus capitis superior and inferior, longus colli, levator scapulae

pearl: Jefferson (burst) fracture from axial loading splays the lateral masses on open-mouth view; unstable if the transverse ligament ruptures (lateral mass overhang >7 mm).

name: Axis (C2) with dens
function: C2 bears the dens (odontoid process), the pivot around which the atlas and skull rotate at the atlanto-axial joints.

details.label: Articulates with
details.value: Atlas (lateral masses and anterior arch via the dens), C3

details.label: Key features
details.value: Dens, large bifid spinous process, superior articular facets, pars interarticularis, transverse foramina

details.label: Ligaments
details.value: Transverse ligament of atlas, alar ligaments, apical ligament, tectorial membrane

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Obliquus capitis inferior, rectus capitis posterior major, longus colli, semispinalis cervicis

pearl: Odontoid fractures: type II (base of dens) is commonest and prone to nonunion in the elderly. Hangman fracture = bilateral C2 pars fracture from hyperextension.

name: Typical cervical vertebra (C3–C6)
function: Small body, large triangular canal, bifid spinous process and transverse foramina; forms the flexible cervical column protecting the cord and vertebral arteries.

details.label: Articulates with
details.value: Adjacent vertebrae via intervertebral discs, uncovertebral joints (Luschka) and facet joints

details.label: Key features
details.value: Transverse foramen, anterior and posterior tubercles, bifid spine, uncinate processes, facets angled ~45°

details.label: Foramina & contents
details.value: Transverse foramen – vertebral artery and vein, sympathetic plexus; intervertebral foramen – spinal nerve root

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Longus colli, scalenes, levator scapulae, splenius, semispinalis, multifidus

pearl: Cervical roots exit above the same-numbered vertebra, so a C5–C6 disc herniation compresses the C6 root: weak biceps/wrist extension, reduced biceps reflex, thumb numbness.

name: Vertebra prominens (C7)
function: Transitional vertebra with a long non-bifid spinous process that is the first easily palpable midline bump at the base of the neck.

details.label: Articulates with
details.value: C6 above, T1 below

details.label: Key features
details.value: Long non-bifid spinous process; small transverse foramen carrying only a vein (vertebral artery enters at C6)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Stellate ganglion anterior to the C7 transverse process/neck of 1st rib; subclavian artery; apex of lung

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Trapezius, rhomboid minor, splenius, serratus posterior superior, ligamentum nuchae

pearl: A cervical rib from C7 can cause thoracic outlet syndrome (ulnar paresthesia, hand wasting, arm claudication). Stellate ganglion injury at this level gives Horner syndrome.

name: Atlanto-occipital joint
function: Paired condylar synovial joints between the occipital condyles and atlas lateral masses; allow flexion-extension (nodding 'yes') and slight lateral flexion.

details.label: Articulates with
details.value: Occipital condyles and the superior articular facets of C1

details.label: Key features
details.value: Convex condyles in concave facets; anterior and posterior atlanto-occipital membranes

details.label: Ligaments
details.value: Alar ligaments and tectorial membrane limit motion; vertebral artery and C1 nerve pierce the posterior membrane

details.label: Movements
details.value: About 15° flexion-extension, minimal rotation

pearl: Atlanto-occipital dislocation (high-energy deceleration, children) is often lethal; survivors show brainstem and lower cranial nerve deficits. Check the basion–dens interval on CT.

name: Atlanto-axial joint
function: Three synovial joints (median pivot around the dens, two lateral gliding joints) that provide about half of all cervical rotation ('no' movement).

details.label: Articulates with
details.value: Dens with the anterior arch of atlas and the transverse ligament; lateral masses of C1 on the superior facets of C2

details.label: Key features
details.value: Median pivot joint; no intervertebral disc between C1 and C2

details.label: Ligaments
details.value: Transverse ligament of atlas (prevents anterior subluxation), alar ligaments (check rotation), apical ligament

details.label: Movements
details.value: About 45° rotation to each side

pearl: Atlanto-axial instability from transverse ligament laxity in rheumatoid arthritis and Down syndrome: screen with flexion-extension films before intubation or surgery.

name: Transverse foramina (vertebral artery)
function: Openings in the cervical transverse processes that channel the vertebral artery, vein and sympathetic fibers from C6 up to the atlas and foramen magnum.

details.label: Location
details.value: Transverse processes of C1–C7 (C7 usually carries only the vein)

details.label: Contents
details.value: Vertebral artery (enters at C6), vertebral venous plexus, sympathetic plexus from the inferior cervical/stellate ganglion

details.label: Course
details.value: Artery ascends C6 to C1, loops over the posterior arch of atlas, pierces the dura and enters the foramen magnum

details.label: Related
details.value: Uncinate processes and uncovertebral osteophytes border them anteromedially

pearl: Vertebral artery dissection after neck manipulation or trauma: neck pain plus posterior circulation stroke (vertigo, ataxia, lateral medullary syndrome).

name: Pterion
function: H-shaped junction of frontal, parietal, temporal and sphenoid bones at the thinnest part of the lateral skull; overlies the anterior branch of the middle meningeal artery.

details.label: Location
details.value: About 4 cm above the zygomatic arch and 3 cm behind the frontozygomatic suture

details.label: Bones
details.value: Frontal, parietal, squamous temporal, greater wing of sphenoid

details.label: Deep relations
details.value: Anterior division of the middle meningeal artery (from foramen spinosum); Broca area on the left

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Covered by temporalis and temporal fascia

pearl: A blow to the temple fractures the pterion and tears the middle meningeal artery: epidural hematoma with lucid interval and a lens-shaped CT bleed that respects sutures.

name: Mastoid process
function: Conical projection of the temporal bone behind the ear filled with air cells; anchors the sternocleidomastoid and neck extensors.

details.label: Location
details.value: Posteroinferior temporal bone, behind the external acoustic meatus

details.label: Key features
details.value: Mastoid air cells communicate with the middle ear via the antrum; mastoid notch (digastric); sigmoid sinus on its inner surface

details.label: Foramina & contents
details.value: Mastoid foramen – emissary vein to sigmoid sinus; stylomastoid foramen (CN VII) lies anteromedially

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Sternocleidomastoid, splenius capitis, longissimus capitis, posterior belly of digastric

pearl: Mastoiditis after otitis media: postauricular tenderness and a protruding ear; may erode to sigmoid sinus thrombosis or brain abscess. CN VII lies just anterior in mastoid surgery.

name: Styloid process
function: Slender spine projecting anteroinferiorly from the temporal bone; a 2nd-arch (Reichert cartilage) derivative that anchors three muscles and two ligaments, forming the styloid apparatus.

details.label: Location
details.value: Below the external acoustic meatus, deep to the parotid, between the ICA (medial) and ECA (lateral)

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Stylohyoid, styloglossus, stylopharyngeus; stylohyoid and stylomandibular ligaments

details.label: Relations
details.value: CN VII exits just posterior (stylomastoid foramen); CN IX, X, XI, XII and internal jugular vein lie medial

details.label: Embryology
details.value: Second pharyngeal arch (Reichert cartilage), with the stylohyoid ligament and lesser horn of hyoid; of its muscles only stylohyoid is 2nd arch (CN VII): stylopharyngeus is 3rd arch (CN IX), styloglossus is from occipital somites (CN XII)

pearl: Eagle syndrome: an elongated styloid (>3 cm) or calcified stylohyoid ligament causes throat and ear pain on swallowing or head turning and may compress the carotid.

name: Zygomatic arch
function: Bony bridge formed by the temporal process of the zygomatic bone and the zygomatic process of the temporal bone; origin of the masseter.

details.label: Location
details.value: Lateral face from the cheekbone to the articular tubercle just in front of the ear

details.label: Key features
details.value: Temporal fascia attaches above, masseter below; temporalis tendon passes deep to it to the coronoid process

details.label: Relations
details.value: Temporal branches of CN VII and superficial temporal vessels cross it; parotid duct runs about 1 cm below it

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Masseter, temporal fascia, zygomaticus major (anterior end)

pearl: Isolated arch fracture: depressed cheek and trismus from coronoid impingement; the temporal branch of CN VII is at risk during elevation, so stay deep to the temporal fascia.

name: External occipital protuberance (inion)
function: Midline bump on the occipital bone at the junction of the superior nuchal lines; attachment of the ligamentum nuchae and trapezius.

details.label: Location
details.value: Midline posterior skull at the level of the superior nuchal lines

details.label: Deep relation
details.value: Internal occipital protuberance and the confluence of sinuses (torcular) lie opposite

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Trapezius, ligamentum nuchae; splenius capitis and SCM along the superior nuchal line

details.label: Key features
details.value: Marks the posterior limit of the scalp and the level of the transverse sinuses

pearl: Landmark for the torcular and transverse sinuses in posterior fossa craniotomy; the occipital artery and greater occipital nerve emerge 2–3 cm lateral (occipital neuralgia block).

name: Sella turcica
function: Saddle-shaped depression on the sphenoid body housing the pituitary gland, roofed by the diaphragma sellae and flanked by the cavernous sinuses.

details.label: Location
details.value: Midline of the middle cranial fossa, above the sphenoid sinus

details.label: Key features
details.value: Tuberculum sellae, hypophyseal fossa, dorsum sellae, anterior and posterior clinoid processes

details.label: Relations
details.value: Optic chiasm anterosuperior; cavernous sinus with ICA and CN III, IV, V1, V2, VI lateral; sphenoid sinus inferior

details.label: Imaging
details.value: Enlarged or eroded sella with pituitary macroadenoma; empty sella on MRI

pearl: Pituitary adenoma grows up out of the sella to compress the chiasm (bitemporal hemianopia); pituitary apoplexy gives sudden headache, visual loss and adrenal crisis.

name: Cribriform plate
function: Perforated roof of the nasal cavity (part of the ethmoid) in the anterior cranial fossa through which olfactory nerve fibers reach the olfactory bulb.

details.label: Location
details.value: Floor of the anterior cranial fossa on either side of the crista galli

details.label: Contents
details.value: Olfactory nerve (CN I) filaments through its foramina; anterior ethmoidal nerve and artery at its anterior edge

details.label: Relations
details.value: Olfactory bulb above; superior concha and nasal septum below; orbital plates of the frontal bone lateral

details.label: Key features
details.value: Crista galli gives attachment to the falx cerebri

pearl: Anterior skull base fracture tears olfactory fibers (anosmia) and dura (CSF rhinorrhea, beta-2 transferrin positive); avoid nasogastric tubes, which can enter the cranium.

name: Optic canal
function: Canal in the lesser wing of the sphenoid connecting the orbit to the middle cranial fossa; transmits the optic nerve and ophthalmic artery.

details.label: Location
details.value: Orbital apex, medial to the superior orbital fissure, within the common tendinous ring

details.label: Contents
details.value: Optic nerve (CN II) with its meningeal sheaths and subarachnoid space; ophthalmic artery

details.label: Relations
details.value: Anterior clinoid process lateral; sphenoid sinus and posterior ethmoid cells medial

details.label: Key features
details.value: About 1 cm long; the optic nerve sheath is continuous with the dura

pearl: Traumatic optic neuropathy from canal fracture gives an afferent pupillary defect with a normal fundus. Dural continuity of the sheath is why raised ICP causes papilledema.

name: Superior orbital fissure
function: Gap between the greater and lesser sphenoid wings linking the orbit to the middle cranial fossa; transmits CN III, IV, V1, VI and the ophthalmic veins.

details.label: Location
details.value: Orbital apex, lateral to the optic canal

details.label: Contents
details.value: CN III, IV, VI; V1 branches (lacrimal, frontal, nasociliary); superior ophthalmic vein; sympathetic fibers

details.label: Key features
details.value: Common tendinous ring spans its medial part; CN III, VI and nasociliary nerve pass inside the ring, CN IV, lacrimal and frontal outside

details.label: Relations
details.value: Cavernous sinus lies immediately posterior

pearl: Superior orbital fissure syndrome: ophthalmoplegia, ptosis, fixed dilated pupil and forehead numbness; add vision loss and it is orbital apex syndrome (optic canal involved).

name: Foramen rotundum
function: Round opening in the greater wing of the sphenoid leading from the middle cranial fossa to the pterygopalatine fossa; carries the maxillary nerve (V2).

details.label: Location
details.value: Greater wing of sphenoid, just posteroinferior to the medial end of the superior orbital fissure; medial to the foramen ovale

details.label: Contents
details.value: Maxillary nerve (CN V2); small emissary vein and artery of the foramen rotundum

details.label: Route
details.value: Cavernous sinus lateral wall → rotundum → pterygopalatine fossa → inferior orbital fissure → infraorbital groove and canal → infraorbital foramen

details.label: Mnemonic
details.value: Standing Room Only: Superior orbital fissure (V1), Rotundum (V2), Ovale (V3)

pearl: V2 sensory loss (cheek, upper lip, upper teeth, palate) with intact V1 and V3 localizes a lesion to the rotundum/pterygopalatine fossa, e.g. perineural spread of skin cancer.

name: Foramen ovale
function: Oval opening in the greater wing of the sphenoid joining the middle cranial fossa to the infratemporal fossa; carries the mandibular nerve (V3).

details.label: Location
details.value: Greater wing of sphenoid, posterolateral to rotundum and anteromedial to spinosum

details.label: Contents
details.value: Mandibular nerve (V3), accessory meningeal artery, lesser petrosal nerve, emissary vein (OVALE mnemonic)

details.label: Route
details.value: Trigeminal ganglion → ovale → infratemporal fossa, where V3 splits into anterior and posterior divisions

details.label: Relations
details.value: Lateral pterygoid plate anterior; otic ganglion hangs just below on V3

pearl: Percutaneous radiofrequency rhizotomy for trigeminal neuralgia passes a needle through the foramen ovale to the Gasserian ganglion under fluoroscopic guidance.

name: Foramen spinosum
function: Small hole in the greater wing of the sphenoid posterolateral to the ovale; transmits the middle meningeal artery into the cranium.

details.label: Location
details.value: Greater wing of sphenoid, just anteromedial to the spine of the sphenoid

details.label: Contents
details.value: Middle meningeal artery and vein; meningeal branch of V3 (nervus spinosus)

details.label: Route
details.value: Maxillary artery → spinosum → grooves the inner skull; anterior branch runs under the pterion

details.label: Relations
details.value: Sphenomandibular ligament attaches to the adjacent sphenoid spine; auriculotemporal nerve nearby

pearl: The middle meningeal artery entering here is the vessel torn in epidural hematoma; its embolization is now used to treat chronic subdural hematoma.

name: Foramen lacerum
function: Irregular cartilage-filled gap between sphenoid, temporal and occipital bones; the internal carotid artery passes over (not through) it to enter the cavernous sinus.

details.label: Location
details.value: Skull base at the apex of the petrous temporal bone, medial to the carotid canal exit

details.label: Contents
details.value: Fibrocartilage plug; greater petrosal and deep petrosal nerves unite above it to form the nerve of the pterygoid canal; meningeal branch of the ascending pharyngeal artery; emissary veins (cavernous sinus to pterygoid plexus)

details.label: Relations
details.value: ICA runs across its superior surface from the carotid canal to the cavernous sinus

details.label: Key features
details.value: No major structure traverses it in life; only a meningeal branch of the ascending pharyngeal artery and small emissary veins pierce the cartilage plug. The ICA crosses its roof without passing through it

pearl: Nasopharyngeal carcinoma spreads through the foramen lacerum into the cavernous sinus, producing CN VI palsy (lateral rectus) and facial numbness.

name: Carotid canal
function: Passage through the petrous temporal bone carrying the internal carotid artery and its sympathetic plexus from the neck toward the cavernous sinus.

details.label: Location
details.value: Inferior surface of the petrous temporal bone, anterior to the jugular foramen

details.label: Contents
details.value: Internal carotid artery, internal carotid venous plexus, sympathetic (internal carotid) plexus

details.label: Route
details.value: Enters vertically, turns horizontally anteromedially, exits above the foramen lacerum

details.label: Relations
details.value: Cochlea and middle ear posterolateral; Eustachian tube anterolateral

pearl: Aberrant or dehiscent ICA in the middle ear gives pulsatile tinnitus and a red retrotympanic mass; never biopsy. Petrous ICA injury in temporal bone fracture causes massive epistaxis.

name: Jugular foramen
function: Opening between the petrous temporal and occipital bones transmitting the sigmoid sinus into the internal jugular vein along with CN IX, X and XI.

details.label: Location
details.value: Posterior skull base, posterolateral to the carotid canal and anterolateral to the hypoglossal canal

details.label: Contents
details.value: Anterior: inferior petrosal sinus, CN IX; middle: CN X, XI; posterior: sigmoid sinus becoming the internal jugular vein (jugular bulb)

details.label: Relations
details.value: Styloid process anterolateral; hypoglossal canal medial; glomus (paraganglion) tissue on the jugular bulb

details.label: Key features
details.value: Usually larger on the right (dominant venous drainage)

pearl: Jugular foramen (Vernet) syndrome: lost gag, dysphagia, hoarseness, uvula deviating away, weak trapezius/SCM. Causes: glomus jugulare tumor, schwannoma, skull base fracture.

name: Internal acoustic meatus
function: Canal in the petrous temporal bone opening into the posterior cranial fossa; transmits the facial and vestibulocochlear nerves and the labyrinthine artery.

details.label: Location
details.value: Posterior surface of the petrous temporal bone, at the cerebellopontine angle

details.label: Contents
details.value: CN VII (anterosuperior), nervus intermedius, CN VIII (cochlear anteroinferior, vestibular posterior), labyrinthine artery (from AICA)

details.label: Key features
details.value: About 1 cm long; fundus divided by the falciform crest and Bill's bar

details.label: Relations
details.value: Cerebellopontine angle cistern medially; vestibule and cochlea laterally

pearl: Vestibular schwannoma widens the internal acoustic meatus: unilateral sensorineural hearing loss and tinnitus, later CN VII and V signs; bilateral tumors suggest NF2.

name: Stylomastoid foramen
function: Opening on the skull base between the styloid and mastoid processes where the facial nerve leaves the temporal bone before entering the parotid gland.

details.label: Location
details.value: Inferior temporal bone between the styloid process (anteromedial) and mastoid process (posterolateral)

details.label: Contents
details.value: Facial nerve (CN VII) motor trunk; stylomastoid artery (branch of posterior auricular artery)

details.label: Route
details.value: CN VII then passes forward into the parotid and divides into temporal, zygomatic, buccal, marginal mandibular and cervical branches

details.label: Relations
details.value: Posterior belly of digastric attaches just posterior (mastoid notch); tympanomastoid suture, tragal pointer and digastric ridge are surgical landmarks

pearl: Lesion at or beyond the foramen (parotid tumor, parotidectomy, facial laceration): ipsilateral facial weakness with normal taste, lacrimation and no hyperacusis; Bell palsy (canal) may add dysgeusia or hyperacusis.

name: Hypoglossal canal
function: Canal in the occipital bone above each occipital condyle, anterolateral to the foramen magnum; transmits the hypoglossal nerve to the tongue.

details.label: Location
details.value: Occipital bone, anterolateral to the foramen magnum, above the anterior part of the occipital condyle

details.label: Contents
details.value: Hypoglossal nerve (CN XII), meningeal branch of the ascending pharyngeal artery, emissary vein

details.label: Route
details.value: CN XII descends between the ICA and internal jugular vein, hooks around the occipital artery and runs forward above the hyoid to the tongue

details.label: Relations
details.value: Jugular foramen anterolateral; condylar canal posterior

pearl: CN XII lesion: tongue deviates toward the weak side with atrophy and fasciculations (LMN). Causes include skull base fracture, carotid endarterectomy and nasopharyngeal carcinoma.

name: Foramen magnum
function: Large opening in the occipital bone where the medulla becomes the spinal cord; also passes the vertebral arteries and spinal roots of the accessory nerve.

details.label: Location
details.value: Floor of the posterior cranial fossa between the occipital condyles; basion anterior, opisthion posterior

details.label: Contents
details.value: Medulla and meninges, vertebral arteries, anterior and posterior spinal arteries, spinal roots of CN XI, tectorial membrane, apical and alar ligaments

details.label: Relations
details.value: Clivus anterior; cerebellar tonsils above; atlas below

details.label: Key features
details.value: About 35 mm long by 30 mm wide

pearl: Raised ICP herniates the cerebellar tonsils through the foramen magnum, compressing the medulla (Cushing triad, apnea). Chiari I = tonsils >5 mm below it, often with syringomyelia.

name: Supraorbital foramen
function: Notch or foramen at the medial third of the supraorbital margin of the frontal bone; transmits the supraorbital nerve (V1) and vessels to the forehead.

details.label: Location
details.value: Supraorbital margin about 2.5 cm from the midline, in the mid-pupillary line

details.label: Contents
details.value: Supraorbital nerve (branch of the frontal nerve, V1), supraorbital artery and vein

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Forehead and scalp skin to the vertex, upper eyelid, frontal sinus mucosa

details.label: Alignment
details.value: Supraorbital, infraorbital and mental foramina lie on a vertical line through the pupil

pearl: Supraorbital pressure is a standard central painful stimulus in GCS testing; a supraorbital nerve block anesthetizes forehead lacerations without distorting the wound.

name: Infraorbital foramen
function: Opening in the maxilla just below the orbital rim through which the infraorbital nerve (V2) and vessels emerge to the cheek, nose and upper lip.

details.label: Location
details.value: Maxilla about 1 cm below the infraorbital margin, in the mid-pupillary line

details.label: Contents
details.value: Infraorbital nerve (terminal branch of V2), infraorbital artery and vein

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Lower eyelid, side of nose, cheek, upper lip (inferior palpebral, nasal, superior labial branches). The anterior superior alveolar branch to incisors and canine leaves the nerve inside the infraorbital canal, proximal to the foramen, and descends in the anterior maxillary wall (canalis sinuosus).

details.label: Route
details.value: V2 → foramen rotundum → pterygopalatine fossa → inferior orbital fissure → infraorbital groove and canal → foramen

pearl: Orbital floor (blowout) and zygomatic fractures injure the infraorbital nerve: numb cheek, upper lip and gum; check for enophthalmos and restricted upgaze (trapped inferior rectus).

name: Mental foramen
function: Opening on the outer surface of the mandibular body below the second premolar; transmits the mental nerve and vessels to the chin and lower lip.

details.label: Location
details.value: Lateral mandibular body midway between upper and lower borders, in the mid-pupillary line

details.label: Contents
details.value: Mental nerve (terminal branch of the inferior alveolar nerve, V3), mental artery and vein

details.label: Supplies
details.value: Skin of the chin and lower lip, labial gingiva of the anterior teeth

details.label: Key features
details.value: Migrates to the alveolar crest with edentulous atrophy; opens posterosuperiorly

pearl: Numb chin syndrome (mental neuropathy) is a red flag for mandibular metastasis or lymphoma invading the inferior alveolar/mental nerve.

name: External acoustic meatus
function: S-shaped canal (lateral third cartilage, medial two-thirds temporal bone) conducting sound from the auricle to the tympanic membrane.

details.label: Location
details.value: Temporal bone (tympanic plate), about 2.5 cm long, ending at the tympanic membrane

details.label: Walls & relations
details.value: Anterior wall abuts the TMJ and parotid; posterior wall abuts mastoid air cells; CN VII lies posteromedial

details.label: Sensory innervation
details.value: Auriculotemporal nerve (V3), auricular branch of vagus (Arnold nerve), small contributions from CN VII and IX

details.label: Key features
details.value: Skin with ceruminous glands laterally; pull the auricle up and back to straighten it for otoscopy

pearl: Malignant otitis externa (Pseudomonas in diabetics) erodes through the canal floor to the skull base, causing CN VII palsy; CT shows bony destruction, needs IV antipseudomonals.

name: Malleus
function: Hammer-shaped first ossicle; its handle is embedded in the tympanic membrane and transmits vibration to the incus, beginning ossicular amplification of sound.

details.label: Location
details.value: Middle ear (tympanic cavity), lateral-most ossicle

details.label: Articulates with
details.value: Incus (incudomalleolar joint) via its head in the epitympanum

details.label: Key features
details.value: Head, neck, handle (manubrium) attached to tympanic membrane; lateral and anterior processes

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Tensor tympani (CN V3) inserts on the handle; dampens loud sounds

details.label: Otoscopic landmark
details.value: Umbo and handle visible through the TM; cone of light anteroinferior

pearl: Loss of the normal malleus/cone-of-light landmarks on otoscopy suggests middle-ear effusion or cholesteatoma; ossicular discontinuity after trauma causes conductive hearing loss.

name: Incus
function: Anvil-shaped middle ossicle linking malleus to stapes; its long process ends in the lenticular process that articulates with the stapes head.

details.label: Location
details.value: Middle ear, posterior to the malleus head in the epitympanum

details.label: Articulates with
details.value: Malleus (incudomalleolar joint) and stapes (incudostapedial joint)

details.label: Key features
details.value: Body, short process (posterior, in fossa incudis), long process ending in lenticular process

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Long process has tenuous supply; most prone to erosion/necrosis

pearl: The incus is the ossicle most often dislocated in temporal bone fracture and most often eroded by cholesteatoma; suspect it in post-traumatic conductive hearing loss with an intact TM.

name: Stapes
function: Stirrup-shaped innermost and smallest bone; its footplate sits in the oval window and delivers vibration to perilymph of the inner ear.

details.label: Location
details.value: Middle ear, medial-most; footplate in the oval window (fenestra vestibuli)

details.label: Articulates with
details.value: Incus (incudostapedial joint); footplate held by annular ligament

details.label: Key features
details.value: Head, neck, anterior and posterior crura, footplate

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Stapedius (CN VII) on the neck; smallest skeletal muscle, protects from loud noise

details.label: Nerve relation
details.value: Facial nerve tympanic segment runs just above the oval window

pearl: Otosclerosis fixes the footplate: progressive conductive hearing loss in young adults (often pregnancy-worsened) with Carhart notch at 2 kHz; treat with stapedectomy or hearing aid.

name: Maxillary sinus
function: Largest paranasal sinus, within the body of the maxilla; drains via the ostiomeatal complex into the middle meatus and lightens the skull while humidifying air.

details.label: Location
details.value: Body of maxilla; roof = orbital floor, floor = alveolar process near molar roots

details.label: Drains to
details.value: Middle meatus via hiatus semilunaris (ostium high on medial wall, poor dependent drainage)

details.label: Key features
details.value: Pyramidal; infraorbital nerve runs in its roof; molar/premolar roots in its floor

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Superior alveolar and infraorbital branches of CN V2

details.label: Fractures
details.value: Involved in Le Fort I, II, III and zygomaticomaxillary complex fractures

pearl: Most common site of adult bacterial sinusitis (S. pneumoniae, H. influenzae, M. catarrhalis); unilateral maxillary sinusitis with foul drainage suggests odontogenic source from a molar root.

name: Frontal sinus
function: Paired sinus in the frontal bone above the orbits; drains via the frontonasal duct into the middle meatus. Absent at birth, pneumatizes during childhood.

details.label: Location
details.value: Frontal bone, between its anterior and posterior tables, above the orbital roof

details.label: Drains to
details.value: Middle meatus via frontonasal duct (frontal recess)

details.label: Key features
details.value: Thin posterior table abuts the anterior cranial fossa and dura

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Supraorbital and supratrochlear nerves (CN V1)

details.label: Development
details.value: Not present at birth; appears ~age 6-8, adult size in adolescence

pearl: Frontal sinusitis can erode anteriorly (Pott puffy tumor: osteomyelitis with forehead swelling) or posteriorly causing epidural/subdural abscess or meningitis; needs CT and IV antibiotics.

name: Ethmoid sinus (air cells)
function: Labyrinth of thin-walled air cells in the ethmoid bone between the orbits and nasal cavity; present at birth and the main sinus involved in pediatric sinusitis.

details.label: Location
details.value: Ethmoid labyrinth, medial to the orbit, lateral to the upper nasal cavity

details.label: Drains to
details.value: Anterior and middle cells to middle meatus; posterior cells to superior meatus

details.label: Key features
details.value: Lamina papyracea (paper-thin lateral wall) separates cells from the orbit

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Anterior and posterior ethmoidal nerves (CN V1)

details.label: Development
details.value: Present at birth with the maxillary sinus

pearl: Ethmoid sinusitis spreads through the lamina papyracea to cause orbital cellulitis (proptosis, ophthalmoplegia, pain with eye movement) and can seed cavernous sinus thrombosis; CT and IV antibiotics.

name: Sphenoid sinus
function: Midline sinus within the sphenoid body beneath the sella turcica; drains into the sphenoethmoidal recess and provides the surgical corridor to the pituitary.

details.label: Location
details.value: Body of sphenoid, directly inferior to sella turcica and pituitary

details.label: Drains to
details.value: Sphenoethmoidal recess, above the superior concha

details.label: Key relations
details.value: Optic nerve and internal carotid artery indent its lateral wall; cavernous sinus lateral

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Posterior ethmoidal nerve (CN V1) and orbital branches of the pterygopalatine ganglion (CN V2)

details.label: Surgery
details.value: Transsphenoidal hypophysectomy approach through nasal cavity and sinus

pearl: Transsphenoidal pituitary surgery passes through this sinus; sphenoid sinusitis presents with deep retro-orbital/vertex headache and can extend to the cavernous sinus, optic nerve, or ICA.

name: Anterior fontanelle
function: Diamond-shaped membranous gap at bregma where the frontal and parietal bones meet; allows molding at birth and brain growth, and serves as a window for ICP assessment and cranial ultrasound.

details.label: Location
details.value: Bregma: junction of coronal and sagittal sutures between the two frontal and two parietal bones

details.label: Key features
details.value: Largest fontanelle (~2-3 cm); normally flat and soft with a palpable pulse

details.label: Closure
details.value: Closes by ~18-24 months (posterior fontanelle by ~2-3 months)

details.label: Clinical use
details.value: Cranial ultrasound window for intraventricular hemorrhage in preterm infants

pearl: Bulging fontanelle = raised ICP (meningitis, hydrocephalus, abusive head trauma); sunken = dehydration. Delayed closure suggests congenital hypothyroidism, rickets, Down syndrome, or hydrocephalus.

name: Cranial sutures (coronal, sagittal, lambdoid)
function: Fibrous joints between calvarial bones that permit skull growth perpendicular to each suture; premature fusion restricts growth in that axis and deforms head shape.

details.label: Coronal suture
details.value: Frontal to parietal bones; runs from bregma down to pterion on each side

details.label: Sagittal suture
details.value: Between the two parietal bones, from bregma to lambda along the midline

details.label: Lambdoid suture
details.value: Parietal bones to occipital bone, from lambda down to asterion

details.label: Key landmarks
details.value: Bregma (coronal + sagittal), lambda (sagittal + lambdoid), pterion, asterion

details.label: Fusion
details.value: Normally interdigitate and fuse in adulthood; dura tightly adherent at suture lines

pearl: Craniosynostosis: sagittal fusion gives scaphocephaly (long, narrow; most common); unilateral coronal gives anterior plagiocephaly, bilateral gives brachycephaly. Positional plagiocephaly has open sutures (reposition/helmet). Epidural hematoma is bounded by sutures on CT; subdural crosses them.

name: Orbital floor
function: Thin roof of the maxillary sinus that supports the globe and inferior rectus; formed by the maxilla, zygoma, and palatine bone and carries the infraorbital groove and canal.

details.label: Formed by
details.value: Orbital surface of maxilla (mostly), zygomatic bone, orbital process of palatine bone

details.label: Location
details.value: Separates orbit from maxillary sinus; slopes up toward the orbital apex

details.label: Foramina & contents
details.value: Infraorbital groove/canal with infraorbital nerve (CN V2) and vessels; inferior orbital fissure posteriorly

details.label: Key features
details.value: Thinnest medial to the infraorbital canal, the usual site of blowout

details.label: Attachments
details.value: Inferior oblique originates from the floor just lateral to the nasolacrimal canal

pearl: Blowout fracture: inferior rectus/orbital fat entrapment gives diplopia on upgaze, infraorbital numbness of cheek and upper lip, enophthalmos; check for oculocardiac reflex and repair if entrapped.

name: Hard palate
function: Bony roof of the oral cavity and floor of the nasal cavity, separating breathing from feeding and allowing suction and speech; soft palate attaches posteriorly.

details.label: Formed by
details.value: Palatine processes of the maxillae (anterior 3/4) and horizontal plates of the palatine bones (posterior 1/4)

details.label: Foramina & contents
details.value: Incisive foramen (nasopalatine nerve, V2); greater palatine (greater palatine nerve/artery); lesser palatine (lesser palatine nerves)

details.label: Key features
details.value: Median palatine suture; torus palatinus (benign midline bony exostosis)

details.label: Innervation
details.value: Sensory CN V2 via nasopalatine and greater palatine nerves

details.label: Blood supply
details.value: Greater palatine artery (from maxillary artery)

pearl: Cleft palate = failure of palatine shelf fusion (feeding difficulty, otitis media, speech); evaluate for Pierre Robin or 22q11. Palatal lesions: torus (benign), Kaposi sarcoma (HIV), necrotizing sialometaplasia.

name: Cranial fossae (anterior, middle, posterior)
function: Three stepped compartments of the skull base that cradle the frontal lobes, temporal lobes/pituitary, and cerebellum/brainstem; each has characteristic foramina and fracture patterns.

details.label: Anterior fossa
details.value: Frontal, ethmoid (cribriform plate), lesser wings of sphenoid; holds frontal lobes and olfactory bulbs

details.label: Middle fossa
details.value: Greater wings and body of sphenoid, petrous/squamous temporal; holds temporal lobes, pituitary; foramina rotundum, ovale, spinosum, carotid canal

details.label: Posterior fossa
details.value: Occipital and petrous temporal bones; cerebellum, pons, medulla; internal acoustic meatus, jugular foramen, hypoglossal canal, foramen magnum

details.label: Boundaries
details.value: Sphenoid ridge separates anterior/middle; petrous ridge and dorsum sellae separate middle/posterior

details.label: Key features
details.value: Floors step progressively lower from anterior to posterior

pearl: Basilar skull fracture by fossa: anterior gives raccoon eyes, CSF rhinorrhea, anosmia; middle gives Battle sign, hemotympanum, CSF otorrhea, CN VII/VIII palsy; posterior threatens lower cranial nerves. Avoid nasal tubes.
